title: Converge language-specific builder runtimes and add buildstamp manifest
creator: Amira Patel
description:
Problem: Our mono-repo currently uses multiple, lightly-differing builder runtime images (node-builder, python-builder, go-builder) which diverge in OS patches, language toolchain versions, and preinstalled linting/formatting tooling. This causes long rebuilds, inconsistent caching behavior across teams, and repeated security patch churn.

Goal: Converge to a small set of standardized builder runtime profiles (slim-language, debug-language, and hermetic-language) and introduce a machine-readable 'buildstamp' manifest that records layer hashes, toolchain versions, and cache hints. This will: reduce image size duplication, improve cache hit rates across CI jobs, accelerate cold-starts, and make rollbacks deterministic.

Outcomes / Success criteria:
- Reduce median CI build time for full repo runs by >= 18% (measured on master pipeline) within one sprint.
- Increase cross-project build cache hit rate from ~62% to >= 82% for language install layers.
- Standardize Node/Go/Python linter versions: node: 20.x (ESLint 9.x, Prettier 3.x), golang: 1.21, python: 3.11 (ruff + black pinned).
- Provide a buildstamp manifest file (JSON) emitted by the builder that includes: base_image_tag, layer_hashes (ordered), toolchain_versions, build_args, and cache_hints.

Approach / Workstreams:
1) Audit current builder images and enumerate diff lists for apt/yum packages, language packages, and installed devtools. (ENG-178902: audit complete list)
2) Design slim-language and hermetic-language Dockerfiles with MULTI-platform arguments and reproducible layer ordering. Keep a lightweight debug-language that includes extra diagnostics but is not used in CI cache priming.
3) Implement buildstamp manifest generator as a buildhook in the repo's root docker-build Makefile; manifest schema v1 documented in Confluence (link below).
4) Migrate top-10 longest-running pipelines to new images in a canary rollout and measure latency.
5) Coordinate toolchain upgrades with teams: schedule 1-week compatibility window and provide upgrade guide and automated codemods for ESLint/ruff rules.
6) Add pipeline step to prime remote cache for language-install layers nightly and after base-image updates.

Risks & mitigations:
- Breaks due to linter/toolchain upgrades: mitigation -> opt-in per-team canary, rollback tags for previous images, and provide fix-up PR templates.
- Cache invalidation causing flakiness during migration: mitigation -> dual-write from old and new builders for two days, and run a comparative build against a golden commit.
- Security patch differences during convergence: mitigation -> ensure CVE scan runs for candidate images and gating on severity >= high.

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Buildstamp+Manifest+RFC
- RFC/Design doc: drive.google.com/drive/folders/EXAMPLE_BUILDSTAMP_RFC
- Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12874
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/ci-builds/canary-image-rollout

Rollout plan:
Week 1: Audit, finalize slim-language Dockerfile, and prototype buildstamp generation.
Week 2: Build nightly images, run integration smoke, and start canary on 3 non-critical services.
Week 3: Expand canary to top-10 pipelines, collect metrics, and iterate.
Week 4: Full cutover, deprecate legacy builder tags, update docs and cleanup.

Notes: This ticket is focused on convergence and the manifest; separate follow-up tickets will cover aggressive binary caching (ENG-179100) and buildkit plugin work (ENG-179101).
